review_records.basis: Production evidence preserves source authority across references and relationships. Cross-Suite references do not represent Certifier, Atlas, Registry, Chronicle, Anchor, or Beacon authority as migrating to Attestor.

Attestor authority is bounded to its governed Attestation, evaluation, and resulting Attestor-owned conclusions. The production evidence does not appropriate canonical objects or institutional acts owned by Certifier, Atlas, Registry, Chronicle, Anchor, or Beacon.

The relationship remediation changed serialization to controlled type/target form without materially changing the governed assertion, subject, scope, authority claim, evidentiary proposition, limitations, or uncertainty. A new ATT canonical identity was therefore not required.

The production chain preserves the separate authority domains of Certifier, Atlas, Registry, Chronicle, Anchor, and Beacon. Attestor uses eligible governed evidence without inheriting, replacing, or redefining those institutions' authority.

The Attestation and evaluation chain remain bounded by scope, evidence, limitations, uncertainty, relevant state, and authority. They expressly exclude substantive truth of the underlying Atlas jurisdiction intelligence and generalized trustworthiness.

No individual input automatically determines the Trust Statement. Six eligible governed inputs were admitted through separate Eligibility determinations, a fixed Evaluation Basis was established, and Rule-Constrained Evaluation occurred before the supported Evaluation Outcome and bounded Trust Statement conclusion.

All related governed objects preserve distinct canonical identities. Relationships provide traceability without collapsing ATT-2026-0001, SC-CERT-2026-0001, SREG-2026-0001, CHR-2026-0001, ANCH-2026-0001, BEAC-2026-0001, or TRST-2026-0001 into one another.
Relationships were not used to establish Eligibility. Each material governed input received a separate Eligibility determination before formation of the canonical Attestation and before Evaluation.

The production relationships preserve source authority and institutional ownership. Reference and other relationship semantics provide governed connectivity without transferring authority to Attestor or among referenced Suite institutions.

ATT-2026-0001 remains draft and unpublished, and the production evidence explicitly preserves lifecycle and publication as separate governed dimensions. Nothing in the production record interprets active as published, favorable, permanently correct, or immune from review. References to an active source state are preserved as source-domain state rather than transferred to the Attestation.
notes: The target is currently draft. This determination addresses compliance with the rule's semantic prohibition; it does not represent ATT-2026-0001 as active.

review_records.basis: The production record distinguishes the reason for the relationship-serialization correction from the versioning decision. The remediation is historically preserved, did not materially change the governed assertion, and did not require a successor ATT. Under the established production evidence, ATT-2026-0001 remains V1.0.
notes: This determination is bounded to the documented serialization-only remediation in the first production operation and does not establish a universal rule that serialization corrections can never require version advancement.
Governed Review remains separate from machine Validation.
VAL-LV-005 is recorded as satisfied because the production evidence preserves the controlled meaning of active and does not mischaracterize the draft target as active.
